findings.finding: The PATHEXT fact -- 'A spawn is not a shell. CreateProcess searches PATH but appends only .exe, never the rest of PATHEXT, so a bare pnpm/npm cannot start on Windows, where node's package managers ship as .CMD shims that PATH resolves perfectly well. Spawning what PATH already resolved starts the same file on every platform.' -- is now spelled twice, near-verbatim, in two modules. The code is not duplicated (each module owns one failure policy, as B1.3 argued), but the prose is: seventeen docstring lines over seven lines of code, of which only the last five sentences say what this module's code cannot -- why not the sibling, why only a bare name. The craft's comment rule is 'only what code cannot' and one fact wants one owner.
findings.evidence: diff of the two docstrings: the first four sentences of _spawnable's are executable's with `npm` -> `pnpm` and one clause added; `git show e66623e2` lines 252-268.
findings.ground: craft Lens shape (comments state only what code cannot; explicit over clever is satisfied, so this is prose locality only). Not correctness: both spellings are true and the behaviour is checked.

causes.cause: The mirrored helper carried the sibling's rationale along with its primitive; the pointer to orchflows_tools.executable already makes the shared fact findable, so the restated paragraph is surplus.
causes.smallest_change: Trim _spawnable's docstring to the sentences that differ from executable's: the pointer to scripts/orchflows_tools.executable as the owner of the PATHEXT fact, the opposite failure contract and why (a done has no 'absent' answer), and the bare-name-only rule. observations.text: Mutant M3 (the separator guard in _spawnable deleted, every first word handed to shutil.which) leaves all 16 tests of the two done modules green. That is not a weak-check finding: shutil.which on a word carrying a separator returns the path itself when it is an executable file, so the existing quoted-absolute-python cases behave identically either way; the guard only changes the refusal text for a missing path-bearing first word (WinError 2 with the guard, 'on no PATH entry' without it). The guard is a stated why-not-the-obvious in the docstring and costs nothing. Noted so a later reader does not mistake M3's survival for an uncovered branch.

Pre-existing, outside Goal: an UNQUOTED Windows path as the first word is mangled by shlex.split in POSIX mode (backslashes eaten), so `C:\Users\...\python.exe -c 1` now reaches the new refusal naming the mangled word `C:UsersdanhmAppData...python.exe`. Before this revision the same input died as [WinError 2]; both fail, and the new text at least shows the author what was searched for. Every existing predicate quotes its path, and the spec prescribes bare tool names. Successor at most: a refusal that quotes the original word beside the resolved one, or a Windows-aware split; either is outside this ticket's surface.

B1.3.repair.1 is an empty commit (no file in `git show --stat`), the craft's 'explicit empty-set proof'. My run_required reading here is a fourth watched green at the same tree 784e3fc1d3db. The single red that opened the round remains unexplained; the repair's friction (the reading's 4000-char stdout/stderr is discarded by verification_line at the moment it is the only evidence) is the successor that would make the next such red diagnosable. Not this unit's defect.
